ink.purpose: The ground of everything. html, body, sheet, map background, mobile detail sheet. Never a lighter page colour.

ink-2.purpose: One step up from the ground for sub-surfaces that belong to the ground, not to pasted stock. Table header, search field, row hover, action bar, country switcher.

stock.purpose: A pasted physical sheet, not a background. One-question panel, check-answers block, selected picker tile, map tooltip, map label plates.

on-ink.purpose: Identical value to stock. Same ink, same paper.

fit-0.purpose: Worst fifth of the live ranking, by quantile.

fit-4.purpose: Best fifth of the live ranking, by quantile. Same value as z5.

z5.purpose: Not a band in practice. The app's counting red: rank badges, slider thumb, verdict score, in-panel focus ring, the share button.

signal.purpose: The single action colour. The two 3px bracket rules, the primary button, the active view tab, step numbers, footer headings, the U in the wordmark.

check.purpose: The only colour outside the green/warm/zone families. Marks one thing: residents were actually researched for this place.

sink.purpose: JS-only. The flat plate behind an excluded place's score, so 'ruled out' reads as a different kind of thing than a low score.

display.purpose: The answer. The place name on the verdict screen and nothing else. Radio Canada width axis at 75%, weight 700, uppercase.

headline.purpose: The wordmark only. 'Where U Belong' with the U in signal mustard; the <i> is neutralised to normal so emphasis is colour, not slant.

title.purpose: The step head on every screen. 'What matters to you?', the current question label.

subhead.purpose: A place name in a ranked row, the wildcard place, the 'All 4,197' plate heading. 2rem in the mobile detail sheet.

body.purpose: Default copy at normal width. Capped 60ch to 66ch. tabular-nums is on and never turned off.

body-small.purpose: Lede, secondary lines, option labels, search field. Steps up to body size below 761px so touch copy stays legible.

label.purpose: Uppercase +0.07em. Picker group headings, question progress, 'Why, answer by answer', footer headings, view tabs, chips, the whole footer body.

shadows.name: paste-tile
shadows.purpose: A selected picker tile, the moment it flips from an outlined chip to a sheet of stock.

shadows.name: paste-panel
shadows.purpose: The two large stock rectangles: the one-question panel and the wildcard note.

shadows.name: float-label
shadows.purpose: The map tooltip, the only thing that genuinely floats over the flooded field.

motion.name: sheet-up
motion.purpose: The mobile detail sheet sliding up from the bottom edge. The only entrance animation in the system.

motion.name: tip-fade
motion.purpose: The map tooltip appearing and disappearing.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce kills every transition and animation globally. Nothing is exempt.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: The mobile world. Gutter 1.1rem, headnote and lede hidden, controls step up a size, the 27-column table leaves the flow, detail moves to a bottom sheet. Also read in JS via matchMedia as a structural switch.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: Reading width clamps to 880px on pick/ask/result; the action bar left-aligns with fixed button widths.

constraints.name: single-file
constraints.value: one self-contained HTML file per country
constraints.purpose: Fonts (156 KB of base64 Radio Canada), all place data and the map geometry are inlined at build time by src/build_app.py. Roughly 7 MB raw, 1.3 MB gzipped for the US. Anything the design needs must survive inlining: no CDN font, no icon font, no remote image, no runtime fetch.

constraints.name: answer-in-hash
constraints.value: the entire answer lives in location.hash
constraints.purpose: Picks and answers encode to the hash as questionIndex.value pairs joined by underscores. A hash fragment is never sent to a server (RFC 3986 section 3.5), so GitHub Pages can never render a per-result link preview. This is why the 1080x1350 share card exists, and why the static 1200x630 og image is generic rather than per-result.

constraints.name: canvas-display-face
constraints.purpose: The 2D context font shorthand used on the share card carries no width keyword, so the condensed display face on the card is set through the detached canvas element's inline style rather than through ctx.font. It is the one place where the display voice is not applied by the stylesheet.

deadTokens.name: --z1 / --z2 / --z3 / --z4
deadTokens.reason: Defined in :root and referenced by nothing in CSS, JS or HTML. Pairwise identical to --fit-0..--fit-3, which are the live names.

deadTokens.name: --fit-ink
deadTokens.reason: #FFFFFF, referenced nowhere. Fit plates and rank badges use a literal #fff.

deadTokens.name: --ink-3
deadTokens.reason: Consumed once in app.js (the empty-search message) but never defined, so that message falls back to inherited colour.

deadTokens.name: --w on .pname
deadTokens.reason: app.js sets an inline --w per row, meant to carry settlement size on the width axis. No CSS rule consumes it, so table place names all set at the same width.

deadTokens.name: .only-wide / .only-narrow
deadTokens.reason: Responsive display utilities defined in the stylesheet but applied to no element in the markup or the generated HTML.

deadTokens.name: .dh / .dwrap / .rib-k / .ribbon / .pts / .sent / .sr / .sk / .st / .sv
deadTokens.reason: Emitted by detailHTML() in app.js for the place-detail record but carrying no CSS rule anywhere in the shipped file, so the detail column headings, resident sentiment bars and climate-ribbon key render at browser defaults.

deadTokens.name: Radio Canada Big
deadTokens.reason: A second family (40 KB of base64) declared in fonts/faces.css and therefore inlined into every built page, but never referenced by the app's CSS or JS. It exists so src/build_og.py can extract it offline for the static 1200x630 og image.

components.name: Picker Tile
components.description: An unpicked dimension in the seed rack. Outlined, transparent, hard-edged; hover brightens the border to mustard.

components.name: Picker Tile, Picked
components.description: A picked dimension. The tile stops being an outline and becomes a pasted sheet of stock carrying a red rank stamp. State change is material, not a tint.

components.name: Action Bar
components.description: The only persistent control in the app. Sticky to the bottom edge, 3px mustard top rule, safe-area padding. The primary label states what happens next; secondary is a colour absence, never an outlined pill.

components.name: One-Question Panel
components.description: One question, filling the screen, on its own sheet of paper. A pasted stock panel with a red rank stamp, the hint, and the control. Inside the panel the whole text ramp flips to on-stock and focus turns red.
components.html:
1This is your top priority

How cold a January are you willing to live with?

components.name: Check-Answers Row
components.description: The signature result component, borrowed from the GOV.UK check-answers pattern. What you asked for, what this place actually is, the sub-score as a ramp-coloured bar, and an edit affordance, in one boring legible row. Never collapsed behind a click.
components.html:
Why, answer by answer

1WinterMild. I do not want a real winter.Nanaimo is 3.4°C

components.name: Explore View Switch
components.description: Three ways to read one ranking, as a hard-edged segmented control. Active is a solid mustard fill; aria-pressed is the source of truth and CSS mirrors it.
components.css: .ds-vswitch{display:flex;border:1px solid var(--rule-2,#2E5C4A)}.ds-vswitch button{font-family:"Radio Canada",ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;font-size:.8125rem;font-weight:700;color:var(--on-ink-2,#AFC8B8);background:transparent;border:0;border-left:1px solid var(--rule-2,#2E5C4A);padding:.5rem .85rem;min-height:42px;cursor:pointer;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.04em}.ds-vswitch button:first-child{border-left:0}.ds-vswitch button[aria-pressed="true"]{background:var(--signal,#E9B949);color:var(--ink,#0B2A21)}.ds-vswitch button:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--signal,#E9B949);outline-offset:2px}

components.name: Find A Place Field
components.description: The only text input in the product. An ink-panel fill inside a bright rule, no radius, no icon. Typing force-switches the explore view to the ranked list, because a search whose results you cannot see is a dead end.
components.html: <input class="ds-search" type="search" placeholder="Find a place by name" aria-label="Find a place by name" autocomplete="off">

components.name: Ranked Place Row
components.description: The mobile ranking unit. Despite its class name in source (pcard) it is a ruled row, not a card: no radius, no shadow, no panel fill. Rank, name, a solid fit plate in the row's ramp colour, the reason, and the weighted-dimension chips.

components.name: Zone Band Ramp
components.description: The fit ramp as it is meant to be read: five countable printed bands, cold to hot, with hard edges between them. The map paints these same five colours by quantile of the live fit distribution, so every band is always populated.

components.name: Provenance Legend
components.description: How the product says what it does not know. A researched place gets a solid violet square, an unresearched one gets a hatch, and a missing value reads as the two dots StatCan publishes for 'not available'. Never a dash, never a zero, never an estimate.

narrative.overview:
A plant hardiness map floods an entire country in saturated bands to answer exactly one question: what survives where. That is already this product's mechanism, so the map stops illustrating the answer and becomes it. The whole visual world is built out of that one idea. Ground is deep printed ink. Panels are sheets of uncoated warm stock pasted onto the ink. Colour is not decoration, it is classification: five countable zone bands own whole regions of the screen at once.

The surface is a printed sheet, not a dashboard. There are no gradients on any surface, no rounded corners anywhere, no card grid, no illustration, and no imagery of any kind. Rules and hard colour edges do the work that borders, shadows and elevation do in a typical product UI. Density is high but ordered: full-bleed horizontal rules, generous vertical rhythm, and one loud thing per screen.

This world was chosen against two specific alternatives, and both refusals are load-bearing. The category default is a white sidebar of sliders over a pale choropleth (MoveMap, Where Might I Live). Its predictable opposite is the cream-ground editorial data essay, which is literally what this app used to be before this rebuild. Both were rejected as the same rut: a quiet neutral field with data politely arranged on top of it. Reaching for either is undoing the decision, not iterating on it.
keyCharacteristics: Deep printed-green ink ground (ink), never a white or cream page.
Warm uncoated stock (stock) used as pasted-on panels, never as the page.
A five-band fit ramp, cold to hot, classed so every band is populated.
Mustard (signal) as the single action colour, used sparingly.
One typeface at two widths. The 75% width axis is the display face.
Zero border-radius, zero gradients, hard printed edges everywhere.
Thumb-first: a sticky action bar, 44px+ targets, one question per screen.

rules.name: The Ink Is The Page Rule
rules.body: The ground is ink, always. Warm stock arrives only as a discrete pasted panel with hard edges and its own on-stock text ramp. A stock panel that bleeds to the full width of the page and carries the whole screen is a cream editorial essay wearing a costume, and that is the rejected world.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Mustard is the action colour and only the action colour. Two mustard things competing on a screen means one of them is not an action.

rules.name: The Live Ramp Is --fit-* Rule
rules.body: The CSS defines the zone ramp twice: --z1 through --z5, and --fit-0 through --fit-4, pairwise identical in value. Only the --fit-* names are live. app.js reads them by literal string through getComputedStyle, so the map field, the table fit plate, the mobile score chip and the check-answers bars are all driven by --fit-*. --z1 through --z4 are referenced by nothing at all; --z5 survives only as the UI counting red. Editing --z1..--z4 changes nothing. Change --fit-0..--fit-4 to move the ramp, and keep --z5 in step with --fit-4 by hand.

rules.name: The Quantile Rule
rules.body: Bands are cut by quantile of the live fit distribution, not by raw score. A palette change must preserve five clearly countable steps, because the map's claim is that you can count the zones.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: The display voice is a width axis, not a second family. Never add a condensed or slab display font to get a bigger headline. The page ships as a single self-contained file with the font inlined as base64, so a second family is real weight on every load.

rules.name: The Uppercase Display Rule
rules.body: Everything in the display voice is uppercase with letter-spacing -0.015em and line-height 0.92. Tight, stacked, and set in caps is what makes it read as printed signage rather than as a big paragraph.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on body and is never turned off. Every ranking, score, temperature and count in this product is meant to be scanned in a column.

rules.name: The Paste Rule
rules.body: A shadow in this system means 'this is stock on top of ink'. If a surface is not stock-coloured, it gets no shadow. Ink-coloured sub-surfaces separate by value alone.

rules.name: The No Lift Rule
rules.body: Nothing rises on hover. Hover changes colour or border, never transform, never shadow depth. The only motion in the entire system is the mobile sheet sliding up and the map tooltip fading.

dos: Do keep ink (#0B2A21) as the page ground on every screen and every new surface.
Do introduce a new light surface as a pasted stock panel with hard edges, the paste shadow, and the full on-stock / on-stock-2 / on-stock-3 text ramp.
Do drive any fit-coloured element from --fit-0 through --fit-4, and keep z5 equal to fit-4 if you retune the ramp.
Do class any new banded visualization by quantile of the live distribution, so every band stays populated and countable.
Do write border-radius: 0 explicitly on any new control.
Do reach for the width axis (font-stretch: 75%, weight 700, uppercase) when you need a display voice, and never for a second font family.
Do keep touch targets at 42px minimum and 56px on the primary action, and give every slider a pair of - / + steppers.
Do state the cost. A result surface must show what you give up alongside what you get, uncollapsed.
Do keep everything inlineable. Fonts, data and map geometry ship inside one self-contained HTML file per country, so no new asset may require a network request.
Do use .. for a missing value.
donts: Don't build a white or pale sidebar of sliders over a light choropleth. That is the category default (MoveMap, Where Might I Live) and it is explicitly refused.
Don't retreat to a cream-ground editorial data essay. That is this app's own previous design and it was rejected as the same rut as the first refusal.
Don't add gradients to any surface. The only linear-gradient in the system is a 2px hatch pattern standing in for 'not researched'.
Don't add rounded corners, card grids, elevation scales, hover lift, or imagery.
Don't spend mustard on anything that is not an action.
Don't turn on imageSmoothingEnabled for the zone field. Soft band edges destroy the printed-map claim.
Don't edit --z1 through --z4 expecting the map to change. They are dead aliases; app.js reads --fit-* by name.
Don't collapse the reasoning behind a disclosure. The check-answers rows, the tradeoff line and the provenance notes are visible by default on purpose.
Don't put a fit score on the share card.
Don't add a second font family, an icon font, or any remote asset.
Don't rely on a per-result link preview. The answer lives in the URL hash, which never reaches a server, which is exactly why the share card exists.
